description: One short script over one input file, in a small repository of a rowing club's boathouse scripts (an existing crew_list.py, sample exports, a README saying the Raspberry Pi has plain python3 only, two commits). The ticket asks for scripts/boat_hours.py: read the boat log CSV (date,boat,crew,out,in; crews quoted when they list several people; in empty while a boat is out; SERVICE rows for workshop days) named as its one argument and print one line per boat with its time on the water this season as H:MM (examples 132:05 and 7:40), most first and equal times by name, with `service due` at 100 hours or more since its last service; it names no technique. The simplest sequential code is right: one pass, two dictionaries, a sort. Required: script_correct (the fixture's sample, three hand-made logs for exactly 100:00 and 99:59 since a service, several services, ties by name, names with spaces, quoted crews, an outing still out, and a generated season of about 2,400 outings; all chronological, and every boat that reaches 100 hours has a service in its log, so every reading of 'since its last service' agrees; exit 0 and the reference's lines, trailing spaces and blank lines ignored). Measures: concurrency constructs in the script, counted from its syntax tree so comments and strings never count (asyncio, async def, await, threads, processes, concurrent.futures and gather), each kind as a flag, code lines, imports and whether they are standard library, the season's seconds, other files changed, tests added, commits. Pass rates cannot record needless machinery here, so qualify/README.md fixes beforehand how a comparison reads the construct and code-line measures. Agent code runs only in bubblewrap. Needs bubblewrap and python3 at /usr/bin or /usr/local/bin; agent arms need no readable entries. See qualify/README.md.
prompt: Could you write scripts/boat_hours.py for the boathouse Pi? It takes the boat log (a CSV export like samples/boatlog-2026.csv) as its only argument and prints one line per boat with how long it has been out on the water this season, most first (equal times by boat name), in hours and minutes, like `Wotan 132:05` or `Libelle 7:40`. If a boat has been out 100 hours or more since its last service, put `service due` after it: `Wotan 132:05 service due`. Service visits are the rows with SERVICE in the crew column, and they aren't time on the water. Outings that are still out (no `in` time yet) don't count. The Pi only has plain python3.
